description: Mix shift: 30% of desktop sessions move to mobile
note: Each device's own conversion_rate/AOV is held at its real (whole-device, that date) value: desktop loses sessions/transactions/revenue in the same proportion (preserves its own rate exactly); mobile gains sessions at its own real rate. Total sessions unchanged. Implemented in evaluation/injector.py's _move_sessions, using largest-remainder rounding (_largest_remainder_round), not plain round() -- see pass_condition_revision.
dates_revision: unchanged 2026-09-27 -- verified via full injection simulation (with the corrected mechanism) that the revised device-dimension condition transfers cleanly on all 5 original dates, no re-screen needed.

device.description: mix is an exact identity (unchanged, always true by construction). Neither desktop's nor mobile's own within-effect reaches verdict=strong -- replaces '|within_total|/|blend_delta| < 10%; desktop/mobile within-share each < 10pt'.

pass_condition.channel_and_country: no pass/fail check -- unchanged limitation: per-dimension decomposition cannot see the true cause lives in a different dimension (device), so a device-level mix shift leaks into channel/country's own within terms. Expected to show one or more segments with a plausible-looking rate change.

pass_condition_revision: revised 2026-09-27: the %-threshold design assumed low real within noise, but device-level conversion_rate has real day-to-day CV ~0.44 (notes/baseline.md dispersion table) even with NO injection -- confirmed desktop's real, uninjected within-share was already 73%-199% of blend_delta on all 5 dates before any mix shift was applied. A verdict-based check absorbs that noise correctly since BH/q already discounts it; a raw %-share does not. Verified via full simulation: desktop lands on material_but_uncertain (never strong), mobile on material_untested/immaterial, on all 5 original dates. See notes/PLAN.md 5.2.
